outcome: Spontaneous preterm birth <37 weeks of gestation in the subsequent pregnancy
cohort: 1032 women with 2 consecutive singleton deliveries at a single institution between July 2012 and June 2018, with the first delivery occurring ≥37 weeks of gestation
finding: A second stage of labor of ≥4 hours in the first pregnancy was not associated with an increased risk of subsequent spontaneous preterm birth, and a second stage of labor of ≥7 hours did not appear to be associated with an increased risk of preterm birth after adjusting for mode of first delivery.
mod_finding: A second stage of labor of ≥4 hours in the first pregnancy was associated with a high rate (>70%) of vaginal birth.
gest_age: First delivery occurring ≥37 weeks of gestation
